answer: Make influence cost time, not money: each identity locks stake whose voting weight grows with lock duration and decays on withdrawal. A sybil operator can fund ten thousand fresh accounts, but every fake starts at the summit's base while honest participants' weight has compounded for months — his influence stays shallow with no shortcut. A sudden signal of capital buys nothing: only aging through real time turns a ripple of deposits into voting power. The limit is patience: a well-funded adversary can pre-age farms, and honest newcomers face the same slow ramp.
